rules.description: Commodity-currency relative value pairs: FX futures (6A, 6C, 6N) spread against beta-matched export-commodity baskets. The spread captures the relative mispricing of two claims on the same terms-of-trade factor.

currency_pairs.economic_rationale: Australia is a major exporter of industrial metals, precious metals, and coal. The currency and commodity export basket are both claims on the terms of trade for commodities Australia exports.

basket_composition.GC: Gold (precious metal, directly traded internationally, Australia is a major producer)
basket_composition.HG: Copper (industrial metal, high correlation with Australian mining exports)
basket_composition.SI: Silver (precious metal, traded globally, Australia exports significant quantities)

currency_pairs.declared_gap: Australian coal export exposure is not directly represented. Coal futures do not exist in the R38 layer. This is a material gap: Australian coal exports represent ~3-4% of global thermal coal supply. The basket (GC, HG, SI) captures precious and industrial metals but misses the coal commodity directly.

currency_pairs.economic_rationale: Canada is a major exporter of crude oil and natural gas. The currency and commodity export basket are both claims on the terms of trade for energy commodities Canada exports.

basket_composition.CL: Crude Oil (WTI, highest-volume crude contract, primary Canadian export)
basket_composition.NG: Natural Gas (Henry Hub, Canada exports significant LNG)
basket_composition.RB: RBOB Gasoline (refined energy product, related to crude processing, Canada exports refined products)

currency_pairs.declared_gap: None material. The three energy futures capture the dominant Canadian export mix: crude, natural gas, and refined products.

currency_pairs.economic_rationale: New Zealand is a major exporter of dairy, agricultural products, and livestock. The currency and commodity basket are both claims on the terms of trade for agricultural and pastoral exports.

basket_composition.ZL: Soybean Oil (agricultural commodity, proxies for vegetable oil/fat exports)
basket_composition.ZS: Soybeans (agricultural commodity, proxy for broader crop exports)
basket_composition.LE: Live Cattle (livestock, New Zealand is a major beef exporter)
basket_composition.HE: Lean Hogs (livestock, although pork is smaller component of NZ exports than beef)

currency_pairs.declared_gap: New Zealand dairy exports (butter, milk powder, cheese) represent ~20-25% of export value and are NOT directly represented in the R38 layer. There is no dairy futures contract available. This is a material gap: the excluded dairy component is typically more price-stable than grains/meat and has different term-structure behavior.
